### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**2** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bc6bff5f39c252d18946c824444a8eba47dc6e1b` — the merge of head `c12ba7bd03aaac53090f7d67d5b50950d2b994f6` into base `18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bc6bff5f39c252d18946c824444a8eba47dc6e1b && git checkout bc6bff5f39c252d18946c824444a8eba47dc6e1b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258 c12ba7bd03aaac53090f7d67d5b50950d2b994f6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258 && git merge --no-ff c12ba7bd03aaac53090f7d67d5b50950d2b994f6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 18cd410dc4053cf8983993104e325f0bbef19258
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c12ba7bd03aaac53090f7d67d5b50950d2b994f6`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23335 (body; comments `6157167302` PM claim, `6158973892` dev report, `6159016506` seat ACCEPT), PR #23360 (body, the one bot comment, file list, diff), ADR-0069 on `main` `18cd410dc`, the head's check-runs (three polls plus the six Test Core job logs), and the head by sha only (`git show` / `git grep`). The net diff GitHub serves is byte-identical, index lines aside, to `git diff 6d96721fa c12ba7bd0` (merge-base to head): 6 files, +379 / -6. `main` has not moved on any of the six files since the merge-base.

### ① Derived judgments

**(a) The ruling and the mechanism — holds.** ADR-0069 D3 on `main`: a held session is "gated out of all protected resources until enrollment + verification"; D1: on authenticated requests past expiry, "return `PASSWORD_EXPIRED`". The platform-admin surface is a protected resource, so refusing a held session there is the accepted record applied, not a new boundary. The consult is the gate's one shared decision in substance: `judgePlatformAdmin` (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/platform-admin-gate.ts:147`) calls `evaluateAuthGate(user, '')`, the function `@objectstack/core` exports at `packages/core/src/security/index.ts:247` (re-exported from the root at `packages/core/src/index.ts:64`) and the same function the dispatcher calls at `packages/runtime/src/http-dispatcher.ts:1396`. No decision logic is copied: the judge reads `held.code` and `held.message` and builds the family's envelope. The pathless spelling is the one six other raw families already use — `service-settings` `settings-routes.ts:176`, `service-datasource` `admin-routes.ts:533`, `service-storage` `storage-routes.ts:687`, `plugin-webhooks` `webhook-outbox-plugin.ts:543`, `cloud-connection` (two sites), `runtime/endpoint-policy.ts:421` — all `evaluateAuthGate(x, '')`. The pathless call is safe, read on the head: `isAuthGateAllowlisted` opens with `if (!rawPath) return false;` (`auth-gate.ts:359`) and the parameterised arm's `matchParameterisedRoute` returns `null` on a falsy path, so the empty path is never allow-listed; `evaluateAuthGate` (`auth-gate.ts:370-375`) is `normalizeAuthGate(user)` then `isAuthGateAllowlisted(path, method)`, so with `''` the answer is exactly the user's posture and no path-dependent exemption can leak in. The posture is present at the judge: `customSession` stamps `authGate` on the same session-user object it stamps `isPlatformAdmin` on (`auth-manager.ts:4119`), and every mount reads that session through `getSession(inProcessSessionReadInput(...))`. Dependency edge: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` already lists `@objectstack/core` in `dependencies` and 13 source files import from it; `@objectstack/core` depends only on `spec` and `types`, so no new edge and no cycle.

**(b) Coverage — complete for the judged family; the gap is the card's own.** Every caller of `judgePlatformAdmin` on the head is in `auth-plugin.ts` (directly or via the hoisted `gateAdmin` at `:2706`): `admin/oauth2/toggle-disabled` (`:2646`), `admin/sso/register` (`:2744`), `admin/unlock-user` (`:2776`), `admin/set-user-manager` (`:2812`), `admin/create-user` (`:2877`), `admin/ban-user` (`:2946`), `admin/unban-user` (`:2967`), `admin/remove-user` (`:3039`), `admin/set-user-password` (`:3127`), `admin/import-users` (`:3146`), `organization/add-member` (`:3209`), `admin/sso/register-saml` (`:3237`), `admin/sso/request-domain-verification` (`:3265`), `admin/sso/verify-domain` (`:3283`) — fourteen mounts, no admin mount registered in any other plugin-auth file. All fourteen now refuse a held session. Admin-ish actions that do not pass the judge: (1) the vendor-served impersonation action, re-authorized by `applyPlatformAdminImpersonation` on the `isPlatformAdminUserId` oracle, which reads stored standing and never the posture — measured by the dev admitting a held platform admin in both states and minting an unheld session; (2) the SSO-provider registration before-hook on the vendor path (`auth-manager.ts:2152`), same oracle, unmeasured; (3) the remaining vendor admin-plugin actions on the legacy role scalar, unmeasured; (4) `admin/has-permission` (`:3090`), which reads `isPlatformAdminUser` without posture and answers a held admin's permission query — a read, noted in the PR's acceptance notes. The seat's `Part of` reading is correct: the card's subject is "a held platform admin may reach user administration", and (1) is user administration on the platform-admin surface, so the card stays open for that leg; the `Part-of PR must not also close its card` check is green. Nothing in this PR is made worse by leaving it: the diff does not touch those predicates, and the vendor-served action admitted a held admin before this change exactly as it does after.

**(c) Order and answers — holds and is stated.** The judge now runs identity (`!user?.id` → 401 `UNAUTHENTICATED`), then posture (403 with the gate's `code`/`message`), then rung (403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`), the order REST (`rest-server.ts:2345-2370`: anonymous-deny, then the gate, then permission) and the dispatcher apply. A held non-admin therefore moves from `PERMISSION_DENIED` to the posture code at the same 403 — stated in the changeset, the PR body, the judge's doc comment and pinned in both tests; acceptable, since the posture is what any held signed-in caller is told at every other seam. The envelope is `{ success: false, error: { code, message } }`, the family's declared `PlatformAdminRefusal` shape (`platform-admin-gate.ts:56-59`); the status set stays `{401, 403}`, so `vendor-admin-refusal-envelope.ts`'s `NORMALIZED_REFUSAL_STATUSES` remains exact.

**(d) Remediation and anonymous — unchanged, verified on the diff.** The `auth-gate.ts` hunk replaces two comment lines with ten comment lines inside `matchesAllowlistedRoute`; the executable early-return for a path with a segment after `auth` (`return true` at `auth-gate.ts:307`) and every other statement are untouched, so `isAuthGateAllowlisted` and, through it, `shouldDenyAnonymous` (`anonymous-deny.ts:67,180`) keep their behaviour. No remediation endpoint calls the judge (the call-site enumeration above is exhaustive), so change-password, two-factor enrollment, sign-out and sign-in are untouched; the booted pin drives each of them under both held states.

**(e) The pins — would fail on ablation, by reading.** Booted pin `packages/verify/src/held-session-platform-admin.pin.test.ts`: real `bootStack` composition, `OS_AUTH_TWO_FACTOR` set before boot; an unheld-admin control that lands the write and reads the row back; per held state a `beforeAll` guard that refuses to run unless the protected REST read already answers 403 with that state's code (so no refusal below it can be vacuous); then the admin write refused 403 with the code AND `sys_user.manager_id` read back unchanged with system context; the held non-admin on the same mount; two-factor enable 200 with a TOTP URI; change-password reaching its own 400 `INVALID_PASSWORD` (a wrong current password, so the hold stays armed); anonymous sign-in 200; sign-out 200. With the consult removed, the two refusal cases per state (admin write admitted and landed; non-admin back to `PERMISSION_DENIED`) go red and the other nine stay green — 4 red / 9 green, matching the dev's measured ablation. Unit pin `platform-admin-gate.held-session.test.ts`: the four held refusals plus the normalized-posture case go red (5), the 401-first, unheld and non-string-code controls stay green (3) — matching 5 / 3. Placing the booted pin in `packages/verify` is acceptable: `@objectstack/verify` depends on `plugin-auth`, `core`, `rest`, `runtime` and the services the composition needs, while `plugin-auth` cannot depend on `verify`; the file imports only `./harness.js`, so `check:cross-package-test-inputs` has nothing to flag; vitest's default `*.test.ts` glob picks up the `.pin.test.ts` name and `tsconfig.test.json` puts it in front of tsc.

**(f) Semver and ADR-0087 — correct.** See ② for the level. The disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` is the right category: no spec key, export, option, config field, response field or stored shape moves, so nothing is tombstoned and `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite; the gate's one refusal for this category is a migration prescription in the body, and the body's "What changes for you" sentence is operator remediation, not a code rewrite — `Check Changeset` is green three times on this head. Every changeset sentence checks against the head: REST and the dispatcher already refuse a held session (`rest-server.ts:2367`, `http-dispatcher.ts:1396`); the named action list (user creation, password, ban, removal, unlock, manager, import, membership, OAuth-client and SSO administration) maps one-to-one onto the fourteen judged mounts in (b) and omits `has-permission`, which is right; 401 first; held non-admin to the posture code; remediation unchanged. The docs callout is true within its own frame — it describes the seams and "every route family that a plugin or service mounts directly on the host server" — but see ③ flag 1 for the one sentence that reads wider than that frame.

**(g) CI on the head — read once at 2026-10-14T01:58:48Z.** 51 check-runs: 37 completed success, 10 completed skipped (`Auto Label` ×2, `Check PR Size` ×2, `Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Regression Gate (matrix)`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Packed-tarball smoke` ×2, `Temporal Conformance`), 0 failed, 0 cancelled. Non-green at read, all `in_progress`: `Test Core (1/6)`, `Test Core (2/6)`, `Test Core (3/6)`, `Test Core (4/6)`. Everything else is green, including `Check Changeset` (×3), `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, all four `Type Check` legs, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Spec property liveness`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Test Core (5/6)` and `Test Core (6/6)`. On `scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts`: it belongs to `@objectstack/spec`'s `test:repo` task (`vitest run --project repo`), whose inputs name `packages/**/*.ts` and `content/**`, so this diff schedules it; shard 1/6's log shows `@objectstack/spec:test:repo: cache miss, executing` from 01:44:14Z, and that shard was still in progress at read, so whether CI ran that file in full is NOT answerable from this read — it will be answered by `Test Core (1/6)`'s conclusion. The owning seat lands only once every check is green (the Tier rule), which includes that shard; no local run substitutes for it.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth`: **minor**, with the `**BREAKING** (an accept-set narrowing)` banner. Correct for this repo at this point: the package is at `18.0.0-next.0`, `.changeset/pre.json` is `{ mode: pre, tag: next }`, and `plugin-auth` sits in the 71-package `fixed` group, so the level cannot change the published number until GA; the banner plus `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` carry the breaking fact into the shipped CHANGELOG, which is what AGENTS.md's changeset rule asks (`(narrowing)` is BREAKING; the ADR-0087 disposition stated in writing). The same `minor` + banner shape is the standing precedent on the head (`.changeset/23015-*`, `23072-*`, `23165-*`, `15953-*`). No FROM → TO is owed: nothing an author can write is removed or renamed.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **Docs sentence wider than enforcement by one vendor-served action (function level).** `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` now says "the platform-admin actions refuse a gated session with the same 403, a platform administrator's included". The vendor-served impersonation action (`applyPlatformAdminImpersonation` on the `isPlatformAdminUserId` oracle) still admits a held platform admin, measured. The lane's disclosure rule keeps the gap out of public text until it lands, so the sentence cannot be qualified today; the landing record on #23335 should name it, and the impersonation leg's PR owns making the sentence fully true. Not a defect of this diff's mechanism.
2. **Mechanism deviation from the claim's file surface, declared and accepted.** The PM claim placed the change in `auth-gate.ts` ("the held-session decision distinguishes remediation from the rest of the auth namespace"); the dev measured that no transport seam sees these raw mounts (the allow-list logged zero calls for any auth-namespace request), so narrowing the arm could not reach them. The consult at the judge is not a new gate (no new decision, list or policy) and widens nothing; `auth-gate.ts` carries a comment only. The claim's "⛔ no new gate / no widening" holds.
3. **Stale comment in the touched file.** `platform-admin-gate.ts:68` still says `judgePlatformAdmin` "(whose bytes are unchanged)"; this diff changes its bytes. Comment-only; a one-line follow-up.
4. **`admin/has-permission` answers a held platform admin's permission query without the posture.** A read, not a write, and by design it refuses no one; it stays outside the judge. Carrier none per the dev; worth a line in the impersonation leg's reading since D3 says "all protected resources".
5. **Unmeasured same-family legs, for the open card.** The SSO-provider registration before-hook on the vendor path (`isPlatformAdminUserId`, no posture) and the vendor admin-plugin actions judged on the legacy role scalar; neither is touched here, neither measured.
6. **`scripts/build-schemas-check-mode.test.ts` not measured locally by the dev** (foreground cap, exit 124 twice); the diff touches no `packages/spec` file. CI's answer is in (g).
7. **Pre-existing order inside two mounts.** `admin/oauth2/toggle-disabled` and `admin/unlock-user` validate the body (400 `INVALID_REQUEST`) before calling the judge, so a held caller with a malformed body sees 400 rather than 403. Unchanged by this diff, leaks nothing, noted for completeness.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23335-held-admin-auth-gate`
Reviewed-by: `session_012uFegdfR6K6uqvLzt7XsdZ`

**VERDICT: PASS**
